terms.definition: Command Line Interface — a text-based interface where you interact with the OS by typing commands rather than clicking a GUI
terms.example: The terminal window you use to SSH into EC2

terms.definition: Print Working Directory — displays the full absolute path of your current location in the filesystem
terms.example: Running pwd in the home directory shows /home/ec2-user

terms.definition: List — shows the contents of a directory. Flags modify behavior: -a shows hidden files, -l shows long format
terms.example: ls -la shows everything including hidden files with full details

terms.definition: Change Directory — moves you into a different directory in the filesystem
terms.example: cd .ssh navigates into the hidden .ssh folder

terms.definition: Make Directory — creates a new folder. The -p flag creates parent directories automatically
terms.example: mkdir -p projects/2025/January creates all three folders at once

terms.definition: Remove Directory — deletes an empty directory. Fails if the directory has any contents
terms.example: rmdir reports deletes the empty reports folder

terms.definition: Remove — permanently deletes files. Use -r to delete directories recursively. No undo or trash bin
terms.example: rm file.txt permanently deletes file.txt

terms.definition: Concatenate — displays the full contents of one or more files directly in the terminal without opening an editor
terms.example: cat authorized_keys prints the SSH public key to the screen

terms.definition: Clears all visible text from the terminal screen without deleting command history. Shortcut: Ctrl+L
terms.example: Running clear gives you a blank terminal to work from

terms.definition: Displays a numbered list of all previously typed commands. Stored in ~/.bash_history across sessions
terms.example: history shows command 1 through 13 from this EC2 session

terms.definition: A file path that starts from root (/) and specifies the full location regardless of where you currently are
terms.example: /home/ec2-user/projects is an absolute path

terms.definition: A file path specified relative to your current working directory — does not start with /
terms.example: projects/2025 is a relative path (valid only if you're in /home/ec2-user)

terms.definition: A file or directory whose name starts with a dot (.) — not shown by ls unless the -a flag is used
terms.example: .ssh, .bashrc, .bash_history are all hidden files

terms.definition: A hidden file in the home directory that stores your command history across terminal sessions
terms.example: ~/.bash_history contains every command you've run in bash

terms.definition: A hidden directory in the home folder containing SSH authentication files including authorized_keys
terms.example: /home/ec2-user/.ssh/authorized_keys holds public keys that can log in

terms.definition: A file inside .ssh that lists public keys allowed to SSH into the account. Each line is one public key
terms.example: When you launch EC2 with a key pair, your public key is placed here automatically

terms.definition: The default SSH username for Amazon Linux 2 EC2 instances
terms.example: ssh -i key.pem ec2-user@public-ip

terms.definition: Privacy Enhanced Mail format — the private key format provided by AWS when you create an EC2 key pair
terms.example: your-key.pem is downloaded once at creation and must be kept safe

terms.definition: PuTTY Private Key format — required by PuTTY on Windows. Must be converted from .pem using PuTTYgen
terms.example: Convert key.pem to key.ppk in PuTTYgen before connecting with PuTTY

terms.definition: A directory that exists inside another directory, creating a tree structure
terms.example: projects/2025/January — January is nested inside 2025, which is nested inside projects

terms.definition: The top-level directory in the Linux filesystem, represented by a single forward slash /
terms.example: All paths start from / — there is only one root in Linux

terms.definition: The text shown before the cursor in a terminal, indicating username, hostname, and current directory
terms.example: [ec2-user@ip-172-31-15-240 ~]$ shows user, host, directory, and user type
